report:
Reviewed crates.sage_ir.inference.terminal_obligations against the complete claim and all three ordinary implementation associations. The claim requires that solver substitutions and residual goals remain local during checking, that fallback and a mandatory terminal pass either discharge remaining work or diagnose it before CheckedBody publication, and that incomplete responses do not leave asynchronous work running after return.

InferCtx submit_obligation retains Ready proof/normalization goals with provenance and caller mappings; retry processing recanonicalizes and deduplicates pending goals. ObligationManager ready_indices, pending_indices, wake, and has_pending consistently treat only Terminal entries as finished. apply_query_response copies substitutions and residual goals into the caller transaction, committing successful applications and discarding failures. InferCtx's proof path handles No by diagnostic failure, Maybe by stalling ordinarily but diagnostic failure at the terminal pass, and Yes with a nontrivial residual by retaining that residual ordinarily or reporting that it remains conditional terminally. The normalization path uses the same terminal distinction and commits normalization relations transactionally. Every submitted obligation has initial provenance, so fail_obligation emits a primary diagnostic; recovery from an existing error uses its existing reported diagnostic rather than emitting cascading errors.

finalize first processes ready work, applies deferred-never fallback and final lower bounds, diagnoses and recovers unresolved inference variables, retries goals enabled by those changes, and unconditionally calls terminally_discharge_obligations. That pass retries every pending goal with terminal=true and asserts none remain. finalize then flushes and drains wake/task work. finish asserts no pending obligations, live root branches, runtime tasks, or unpublished wakes before constructing CheckedBody. The additional captured function-body boundary calls finalize immediately before finish. These assertions prevent publication even if a future producer accidentally leaves work alive. Incomplete/ambiguous results therefore become a diagnostic terminal outcome here rather than an outstanding scheduling promise; the captured architectural rationale distinguishes such incompleteness from logical rejection.

The complete associated test set contains one explicit TODO, sage_meta::todo::inference_terminal_obligations. It has no assertions and supplies no executable verification. Its comment accurately defers a focused matrix for immediate solution, inference-triggered wakeup, recanonicalization/deduplication, terminal rejection, deterministic resource exhaustion, and final absence of obligations/tasks/wakes/root branches. Completing that test evidence requires controlled solver/body fixtures for those scenarios and observable completion-state assertions, particularly configured resource-limit exhaustion. This is accepted as an explicit test deferral, not tested completion. No ordinary associated test is being claimed sufficient. This review does not remove or relabel the TODO.

Added only essential association comments in infer/obligations.rs and solve/boundary.rs, then restarted and inspected the fresh association inventory. Source inspection establishes the current terminalization flow; it is separate from execution. Executed cargo fmt and cargo build successfully (existing compiler warnings), and cargo test -p sage-ir --lib check::infer_ctx::tests: four passed. Those helper tests are supplementary checks and do not discharge the deferred terminal-obligation matrix. Centralized post-codegen and Sage sanity delegation remains with the coordinator as captured in its instructions.
